## Scientific And Domain Assessments

### MREC: stored-and-virtual-search

evidence: supported. Targets: AIMech:MREC.

EXPLORE and UPDATE distinguish stored expansion from virtual recursive traversal. The accepted wording preserves the absence of an OPEN list without asserting that every visited state remains stored.

### MREC: retained-graph-estimates

evidence: supported. Targets: AIMech:MREC.

EXPAND creates a heuristic-initialized node only for a newly stored successor and otherwise adds an edge to the existing node. UPDATE distinguishes its stored estimate from the heuristic used for an unstored successor.

### MREC: inclusive-recursion-and-backup

evidence: supported. Targets: AIMech:MREC.

The operational test follows the displayed inclusive comparison and passes a cost-subtracted bound. Normal completion performs the minimum backup; the goal-found return bypasses those final assignments. The conflicting strict comparison in the prose remains a limitation.

### MREC: extra-memory-control

evidence: supported. Targets: AIMech:MREC.

M measures additional graph storage beyond the recursion stack. The zero-additional-storage IDA* endpoint and the ample-storage difference from OPEN-based A* describe scope, without collapsing the full configurable method into either neighbor.

### MREC: limitation 1

scope: supported. Targets: AIMech:MREC.

The additional-memory parameter excludes the implicit recursion stack. Node, edge and runtime overhead cannot be interpreted as a portable byte limit; this is an accounting qualification.

### MREC: limitation 2

scope: supported. Targets: AIMech:MREC.

The visible UPDATE code uses an inclusive comparison while its adjacent prose uses a strict comparison with inconsistent subscripts. The record identifies which presentation defines the operational claim and preserves the discrepancy.

### MREC: limitation 3

scope: supported. Targets: AIMech:MREC.

The source’s admissible minimum-cost statement is reported with the displayed main loop, which repeats until a goal is found. It is not enlarged into solution existence or a general unsolvable-instance termination result.

### MREC: limitation 4

scope: supported. Targets: AIMech:MREC.

Finite-contour, positive-cost and goal-zero assumptions are identified as conditions requiring a separate argument, not as an uninspected theorem in this paper. Infinite spaces, zero-cost cycles and negative costs receive no new guarantee.

### MREC: limitation 5

scope: supported. Targets: AIMech:MREC.

Stored-node reuse and virtual traversal have different retention behavior. The accepted record does not infer a global closed set containing every encountered state.

### MREC: limitation 6

scope: supported. Targets: AIMech:MREC.

The source distinguishes expansion order and potentially the chosen path from A*, and describes an IDA* endpoint. Those relationships do not establish general alias equivalence.

### MREC: limitation 7

scope: supported. Targets: AIMech:MREC.

LIMMARK, the proposed stored-node removal modification and REC_A remain separate follow-ups. The Concluding Remarks locator is retained, and Sen’s uninspected thesis is not used to supply unseen implementation or cyclic AND/OR guarantees.

### MREC: limitation 8

scope: supported. Targets: AIMech:MREC.

The experiments and update overhead establish only the stated source setting. No numerical result, universal speedup or universal memory/time tradeoff is added to the review.

### MREC: defining source scope

evidence: supported. Targets: AIMech:MREC.

The defining evidence is the six-page IJCAI 1989 paper, printed 297–302, with exact original PDF bytes. The accepted source review covered all pages; this preparation reuses that attributed reading. The inclusive UPDATE/prose discrepancy, early goal return and separate variants remain visible; no new download, theorem proof or benchmark replication is claimed.

### Simplified memory-bounded A-star search: best-leaf-and-single-successor

evidence: supported. Targets: AIMech:SimplifiedMemoryBoundedAStar.

The displayed SMA* selects the deepest least-f leaf, tests that selected node for a goal, generates one successor and applies max(parent backed-up f, child g+h). The source order and tie choice are retained.

### Simplified memory-bounded A-star search: completed-node-backup

evidence: supported. Targets: AIMech:SimplifiedMemoryBoundedAStar.

BACKUP is invoked when the selected node is completed. Its body also requires a parent, and upward recursion occurs only after the value changes under the same guard. OPEN removal requires that all successors are in memory.

### Simplified memory-bounded A-star search: bounded-pruning-and-regeneration

evidence: supported. Targets: AIMech:SimplifiedMemoryBoundedAStar.

The displayed USED&gt;MAX step deletes the shallowest highest-f OPEN node, removes its parent link and can reinsert the parent. Subsequent regeneration uses retained bounds; it does not preserve every deleted descendant value.

### Simplified memory-bounded A-star search: node-budget-and-bookkeeping

evidence: supported. Targets: AIMech:SimplifiedMemoryBoundedAStar.

MAX and USED count nodes. The stated g, h, f, minimum examined-successor f and next-successor fields follow the source bookkeeping description without asserting a portable byte cap.

### Simplified memory-bounded A-star search: limitation 1

scope: supported. Targets: AIMech:SimplifiedMemoryBoundedAStar.

MAX is a node budget. Per-node fields, OPEN structures, backup and transient construction require separate implementation accounting, so the source is not a byte-level memory contract.

### Simplified memory-bounded A-star search: limitation 2

scope: supported. Targets: AIMech:SimplifiedMemoryBoundedAStar.

The optimal-solution statement retains its optimal-path node-budget requirement and the admissibility/pathmax setting. Reporting that statement does not independently prove it or extend it to arbitrary small budgets.

### Simplified memory-bounded A-star search: limitation 3

scope: supported. Targets: AIMech:SimplifiedMemoryBoundedAStar.

Footnote 6 excludes graph transpositions. The tree-search record therefore adds no closed-list, reopening or general state-duplicate mechanism.

### Simplified memory-bounded A-star search: limitation 4

scope: supported. Targets: AIMech:SimplifiedMemoryBoundedAStar.

This is an explicit boundary against extending the source to unrestricted infinite, zero-cost-cycle or negative-cost termination. It asserts neither an unprinted theorem nor a new counterexample.

scope: supported. Targets: AIMech:SimplifiedMemoryBoundedAStar.

The retained ancestor bound can be weaker than information formerly held at a deleted descendant. The narrative preserves that regeneration loss without converting the example into a new performance claim.

### Iterative threshold search: branch-state-before-child-generation

evidence: supported. Targets: AIMech:IterativeThresholdSearch.

Install represents applicable operators as branches before invoking them to generate children, initializes their bounds with the installed node’s g+h, and creates a dummy branch when no operator applies.

### Iterative threshold search: threshold-and-leftmost-selection

evidence: supported. Targets: AIMech:IterativeThresholdSearch.

The outer threshold is the minimum tip-branch bound. Selection uses the leftmost tip branch within that threshold and tests its parent for a goal; the narrative does not move the test to an ungenerated child.

### Iterative threshold search: retraction-and-bound-backup

evidence: supported. Targets: AIMech:IterativeThresholdSearch.

Retraction requires at least S stored nodes and at least two tip nodes. It prefers the leftmost tip node with all outgoing bounds above the threshold and otherwise uses the rightmost tip. The incoming branch receives the minimum outgoing bound before the node and outgoing branches are removed.

### Iterative threshold search: minimum-storage-keeps-active-path

evidence: supported. Targets: AIMech:IterativeThresholdSearch.

The source’s S=0 setting keeps the current path while retracting other nodes. This is a node-storage control rule with branch and operator state, not zero total memory or a strict zero-node capacity.

### Iterative threshold search: limitation 1

scope: supported. Targets: AIMech:IterativeThresholdSearch.

The storage model counts nodes and protects the current path through the two-tip guard. The S=0 example still requires path, branch and operator storage.

### Iterative threshold search: limitation 2

scope: supported. Targets: AIMech:IterativeThresholdSearch.

The Background’s strict h(n)&gt;0 display conflicts with Example 1’s h=0 setting. Under the separately stated nonnegative, admissible interpretation with zero remaining cost at a goal, h(goal)=0 follows; this inference does not follow from the literal strict-positive display.

### Iterative threshold search: limitation 3

scope: supported. Targets: AIMech:IterativeThresholdSearch.

Theorem 2 is retained as a source statement whose proofs are referred to an uninspected thesis. The review supplies no all-input termination proof or invented finite-contour/positive-cost premises.

### Iterative threshold search: limitation 4

scope: supported. Targets: AIMech:IterativeThresholdSearch.

The underlying problem graph and the maintained search tree are different representations. The inspected ITS procedure does not thereby establish transposition detection or reopening rules.

### Iterative threshold search: limitation 5

scope: supported. Targets: AIMech:IterativeThresholdSearch.

Theorem 4 requires the same left-to-right operator order. Its node-generation comparison is not a universal runtime statement and need not cover changed ordering.

### Iterative threshold search: limitation 6

scope: supported. Targets: AIMech:IterativeThresholdSearch.

The constructed finite-tree family and sampled traveling-salesman setting do not establish average-case or asymptotic optimality for arbitrary distributions. No numeric or asymptotic performance result is added.

### Iterative threshold search: limitation 7

scope: supported. Targets: AIMech:IterativeThresholdSearch.

The flow-shop modification ITS-prime(0) in Table 1 remains distinct from standard ITS(0) in Table 2. The review does not transfer the modified method’s results to the standard algorithm.

### Iterative threshold search: limitation 8

scope: supported. Targets: AIMech:IterativeThresholdSearch.

Node-generation savings and runtime differ because bookkeeping also costs time. The source’s counter-overflow and possible-thrashing warning for the two largest 15-puzzle cases remains explicit, and those results are not treated as clean general performance evidence.

evidence: supported. Targets: AIMech:IterativeThresholdSearch.

## Limits And Additional Notes

- All primary-page and mapping reading is attributed to bound historical research and independent-review receipts. This preparation reads the complete previews and support; it does not claim fresh visual source reading, new downloads or a theorem proof.
- The three parameters have different accounting scopes: M is additional graph storage, MAX is a node budget, and S controls retraction while protecting the active path. None is a portable total-byte bound.
- No numerical benchmark advantage, unrestricted termination, new graph duplicate-detection guarantee, source exhaustion, MA*/MAO* acceptance or IE/RBFS alias decision is asserted.
- The exact 22 bibliography objects with 28 occurrences and 6 search-only leads remain historical pending source accounting. Historical owner links and blank links are preserved, not refreshed by inference.
- No positive AIO mapping is asserted. Twelve examined classes and thirteen native context records retain explicitly attributed historical reading scopes; capture is not fresh scientific approval.
- Actual current metadata must retain 22 bibliography objects/28 occurrences, six search-only leads, MA*/IE residuals and additional current questions, plus all inherited responsibilities.
- Actual six creation outputs, one CREATE history, 53 capture inputs and 7 parsed generated pages are bound. Six required commands passed; earlier failed attempts remain explicit. Canonical review save/check and publication are subsequent operations.

limitations:
- All primary-page and mapping reading is attributed to bound historical research
  and independent-review receipts. This preparation reads the complete previews and
  support; it does not claim fresh visual source reading, new downloads or a theorem
  proof.
- 'The three parameters have different accounting scopes: M is additional graph storage,
  MAX is a node budget, and S controls retraction while protecting the active path.
  None is a portable total-byte bound.'
- No numerical benchmark advantage, unrestricted termination, new graph duplicate-detection
  guarantee, source exhaustion, MA*/MAO* acceptance or IE/RBFS alias decision is asserted.
- The exact 22 bibliography objects with 28 occurrences and 6 search-only leads remain
  historical pending source accounting. Historical owner links and blank links are
  preserved, not refreshed by inference.
- No positive AIO mapping is asserted. Twelve examined classes and thirteen native
  context records retain explicitly attributed historical reading scopes; capture
  is not fresh scientific approval.
- Actual current metadata must retain 22 bibliography objects/28 occurrences, six
  search-only leads, MA*/IE residuals and additional current questions, plus all inherited
  responsibilities.
- Actual six creation outputs, one CREATE history, 53 capture inputs and 7 parsed
  generated pages are bound. Six required commands passed; earlier failed attempts
  remain explicit. Canonical review save/check and publication are subsequent operations.
